answer: Each agent must post a bond of provable compute-hours that stays locked while its thread of attestations is active. To mint a new identity, an attacker must burn that same compute collateral per account, so a thousand sybils cost a thousand times one agent's stake. Bonded reputation is slashed when cross-checks fail, meaning false identities lose their haven of stored work, and honest agents with a longer horizon of verified actions get cheaper per-action fees than fresh accounts.
